tip: Από (apó) = than: πιο γρήγορο από (pio ghríghoro apó) = faster than.
After από (apó) the noun takes its object form: από την μπίρα (apó tin bíra) = than the beer.
Την άλλη (tin áli) = the other one, with the noun παραλία (paralía = beach) left out because it is understood.
After από (apó) the pronoun switches to its object form: πιο ψηλός από εμένα (pio psilós apó eména) = taller than me, with εμένα (eména) rather than εγώ (eghó = I).
Πιο (pio) also works with words describing the verb: πιο ωραία (pio oréa) = more nicely, better.
Έχει (ékhi) = there is: έχει φασαρία (ékhi fasaría) = there is noise.
Δικός (dhikós = own) changes ending to match the noun: τη δική μου (ti dhikí mu) = mine, feminine to match η βαλίτσα (i valítsa = the suitcase).
Καλύτερος (kalíteros) = better in one word, no πιο (pio) needed, since πιο καλύτερος doubles the comparison like English 'more better'. Same with χειρότερος (khiróteros = worse).
Καλύτερα (kalítera) ending in -α goes with a verb: νιώθω καλύτερα (niótho kalítera) = I feel better. The -ος form is for describing nouns.
'Worse' is one word: χειρότερη (khiróteri), the partner of καλύτερος (kalíteros = better). No 'more' needed: χειρότερη από ποτέ (khiróteri apó poté) = worse than ever.
Ακόμα (akóma) before a comparison word = even: ακόμα χειρότερος (akóma khiróteros) = even worse.
Μεγαλύτερη (meghalíteri) can mean bigger or older, and context decides: μεγαλύτερη από εμένα (meghalíteri apó eména) = older than me, not bigger in size.
Shoe size is usually νούμερο (número), clothing size μέγεθος (méyethos): σε μεγαλύτερο νούμερο (se meghalítero número) = in a bigger size.
Μικρότερος (mikróteros) covers both smaller and younger: ο μικρότερος γιος (o mikróteros yos) = the youngest son, not the smallest one.
Ο, η or το in front of πιο (pio) makes it the most: το πιο ωραίο (to pio oréo) = the most beautiful.
After a the-most phrase, Greek says of where English says in: το πιο παλιό σπίτι του χωριού (to pio palió spíti tu khoriú) = the oldest house in the village.
Κάνει (káni) with a stretch of time = it takes: κάνει τρεις ώρες (káni tris óres) = it takes three hours.
Καλύτερος (kalíteros) picks up a second accent when μου follows: ο καλύτερός μου φίλος (o kalíterós mu fílos) = my best friend.
Το χειρότερο (to khirótero) = the worst thing: το plus a describing word works as a noun on its own, so no word for thing is needed. Same with το καλύτερο (to kalítero) = the best part.
With verbs use πιο πολύ: μου αρέσει πιο πολύ (mu arési pio polí) = I like it more.
Πιο πολλά (pio pollá) = more in the plural, because the understood word is τα λεφτά (ta leftá = money), which is plural in Greek.
Κατα- (kata-) in front of a color makes it intense: κατακόκκινος (katakókinos) = deep red.
Καφέ (kafé) = brown, taken from 'coffee', and borrowed colors normally keep one form: τα καφέ παπούτσια (ta kafé papútsia) for any gender or number.
Δεν μου πάει (dhen mu pái) is literally 'it doesn't go to me' = it doesn't suit me. Colors and clothes 'go to' people in Greek.
The -ινο ending means made of: ξύλινο (ksílino) = wooden, from ξύλο (ksílo = wood).
Κρατάει (kratái) is 'holds', and a thing that holds, lasts: κρατάει χρόνια (kratái khrónia) = it lasts for years.
Από (apó) before a material = made of: από μαλακό βαμβάκι (apó malakó vamváki) = of soft cotton.
Φοράτε (foráte) is the polite plural, normally used by shop staff even with a single customer: τι μέγεθος φοράτε; (ti méyethos foráte) = what size do you wear?
Χτυπάω (khtipáo) is 'hit', and tight shoes literally hit you in Greek: με χτυπάνε (me khtipáne) = they pinch me.
Δεν μου κάνει (dhen mu káni) is literally 'it doesn't do for me' = it doesn't fit me. For sizes and gear, things 'do' for you in Greek.
